source: Aswath Damodaran, divginzu.xls sheet 'US Industry averages' (NYU Stern, 2020 spreadsheet collection)
as_of_note: Dated to the collection year. The workbook ships in Damodaran's 2020 collection; its companion Country ERP sheet carries a 5.69% mature-market premium from an earlier update, so treat 2020-01 as the latest possible date, not a certified one.
refresh: https://pages.stern.nyu.edu/~adamodar/ - 'Betas by Sector' and 'Industry averages'. Damodaran reposts these every January. Betas, multiples and margins move materially year to year; refresh annually and record which vintage the valuation used.
na_means: NA in the source sheet means the statistic is not meaningful for that industry - margins, sales-to-capital, EV/EBITDA and working-capital columns for banks, brokers and insurers, whose revenue and capital are not defined the way the ratio assumes. Those fields are null here. Null is not zero: never average it in, never plug it.
